business_process: Train dispatching and movement authority (CTC and track warrants)
description: Dispatchers set CTC routes and signals through the CAD/CTC office system, issue track warrants in dark territory, grant track and time to roadway workers, and keep train sheets and bulletins
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No movement authority stops all 26 trains a day; about $537,000 freight revenue per day depends on train movement; manual dispatch in CTC territory has never been drilled (gap 6); after 4 hours trains held at Jacksonville block Class I interchange tracks
manual_workaround: Manual dispatch procedure: paper track warrants and train sheets by radio in all territory, signal maintainers sent to key control points to operate them locally on the dispatcher's instruction, roadway work suspended except emergency work; backup NOC takes over if the primary NOC is affected
dependent_third_parties: CAD/CTC vendor; radio system vendor; leased circuit carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: 36 train dispatchers; primary NOC (HQ); backup NOC (Jacksonville Terminal Yard); signal maintainers
quantified_operational_impact: 26 trains a day; 4 hours down holds about 8 trains; manual dispatch handles about 30% of normal throughput in CTC territory
quantified_regulatory_impact: Dispatch is a Critical Cyber System in the TSA-approved CIP; a cyber incident is reportable to CISA within 72 hours (SD 1580-21-01E II.C) and to TSA within 24 hours (1570.203)
safety_impact_detail: Severe: conflicting movement authority or loss of roadway worker protection during an unpracticed switch to manual dispatch

business_process: Contract dispatching and car management for the affiliated and contracted short lines
description: Company dispatchers run track warrant control for the 2 affiliates (140 route miles) and, from 2027-01-01, the contracted short line; their car records live in the company TMS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Services agreements commit to restoring dispatching within 2 hours; the contracted short line requires a SOC 2 Type 2 report (P09); same safety driver as BP-01
manual_workaround: Affiliates' crews stop and call the company NOC by phone; dispatchers issue paper track warrants by radio or phone from the manual dispatch binder for each affiliate
dependent_third_parties: CAD/CTC vendor; TMS vendor; affiliates' radio and phone carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Dispatchers assigned to the affiliate desks; primary and backup NOC
quantified_operational_impact: 2 affiliate desks; about 9 trains a day on the affiliates; service credits under the agreements after 2 hours
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract obligations; the affiliates' own TSA and FRA duties do not move to the company, but their movement authority does
safety_impact_detail: Severe: conflicting authority on an affiliate's line
regulatory_driver: C-TRANSPORTATION-R01 (SD 1580-21-01E II.C: systems the company operates)

business_process: PTC tenant operations on the trackage-rights segment
description: Initialize and run the 46 PTC-equipped locomotives on the host Class I's line: tenant back office server (BOS), locomotive and crew data, consist loading, message exchange with the host
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without the BOS, company trains cannot initialize PTC and may not enter the host's PTC territory (49 CFR 236.1006(a)); the segment carries about 22% of freight revenue (about $118,000 a day); rerouting through Jacksonville adds about a day
manual_workaround: Hold trains for the segment; reroute priority traffic through the Jacksonville interchange by agreement with the Class I; fail over to the standby BOS at the backup NOC
dependent_third_parties: PTC vendor (managed service); host Class I; industry interoperable messaging network
dependent_people_or_facilities: PTC Program Manager; 3 PTC administrators; backup NOC
quantified_operational_impact: 6 to 8 trains a day on the segment; after 12 hours about 4 trains held or rerouted
quantified_regulatory_impact: Each controlling locomotive on the segment must have an operative onboard apparatus (236.1006(a)); en route failures handled under 236.1029; PTC systems are Critical Cyber Systems (SD 1580/82-2022-01E III.A.2)
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: trains held, not run without PTC; safety risk arises only if procedures are bypassed

business_process: CTC field signal and code line operation and maintenance
description: Signal maintainers keep 150 wayside signal locations, the code line, 38 radio towers, 22 detectors, and 118 crossing monitors working; changes to non-vital communication controllers are made from 3 CTC maintenance workstations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Vital field logic keeps signals safe without the office, but loss of the code line forces manual dispatch (BP-01); controller configurations change rarely, so a daily backup is enough; an unauthorized change to a controller is a safety and regulatory event
manual_workaround: Control points operated locally by maintainers; detector and crossing alarms continue to reach crews by voice radio; restore controller configurations from the signed configuration archive
dependent_third_parties: CTC field equipment vendor; radio system vendor; detector vendor; leased circuit carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: 70 signal and communications staff; 38 tower sites; 150 signal locations
quantified_operational_impact: 150 signal locations; loss of the code line affects 284 CTC route miles
quantified_regulatory_impact: Signal apparatus housings must be secured against unauthorized entry (236.3); field zones must be segmented (SD 1580/82-2022-01E III.B)
safety_impact_detail: Severe: a tampered controller or detector could hide an alarm or mislead a dispatcher, although vital logic still protects signals

description: Crew management application calls crews from boards under the collective bargaining agreements, tracks rest, and keeps hours of duty records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trains cannot be crewed lawfully without rest and hours data; hours of duty records are required (49 CFR 228.11); 330 train and engine employees
manual_workaround: Printed crew boards refreshed every 4 hours; crew callers work from the boards by phone; hours of duty captured on paper forms and entered after recovery
dependent_third_parties: Crew management software vendor; cloud provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Crew callers (in the NOC); 330 train and engine employees
quantified_operational_impact: About 70 crew starts a day; manual calling takes about 3 times longer and causes late starts
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hours of duty records under 49 CFR 228.11; hours of service limits remain in force during the outage
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: fatigue risk if rest data is wrong or missing

business_process: Car management, waybills, and train consists
description: TMS holds waybills, car locations, and train consists; consists feed PTC initialization and train documents, including hazmat car positions
process_owner: Director of Customer Service and Car Management
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trains need accurate consists to depart and to initialize PTC; TMS vendor states RTO 24 hours in its SOC 2 description, longer than this RTO (finding 4)
manual_workaround: Printed consists and paper waybills from the last TMS extract; consist files from the Class I partners by email; train documents prepared by hand from car inspections
dependent_people_or_facilities: 12 car management and customer service staff; yard clerks
quantified_operational_impact: About 590 carloads a day handled; manual consists take about 20 minutes per train
quantified_regulatory_impact: Hazmat train documents and car positions must stay correct; wrong consists cause PTC initialization failures
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: hazmat car position or consist errors

business_process: RSSM location, chain of custody, and TSA reporting
description: Answer TSA requests for the location and shipping information of every RSSM car within 30 minutes; document attended transfers of PIH cars in the Jacksonville HTUA; report significant security concerns to TSA
process_owner: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The 30-minute TSA clock is fixed by regulation (1580.203(d)); the answer depends on TMS car data and dispatcher train sheets; chain-of-custody records kept 60 days (1580.205(h))
manual_workaround: Printed RSSM car list at both NOCs every 4 hours; standby laptop with an encrypted offline extract; train sheets for cars in trains; paper chain-of-custody forms
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat; on-duty Chief Dispatcher (alternate Security Coordinator)
quantified_operational_impact: About 5,200 PIH tank cars a year; on a typical day 40 to 60 RSSM cars are in company custody
quantified_regulatory_impact: Civil penalty exposure for missing the 30-minute duty; 1570.203 24-hour report and the SD 72-hour CISA report run during any cyber incident
safety_impact_detail: Severe: inability to locate PIH cars during a security event

business_process: Interchange with the Class I railroads
description: Exchange cars, interchange reports, and EDI with 2 Class I railroads at Jacksonville and the trackage-rights Class I; attended transfers of PIH cars inside the HTUA
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 70% of carloads move through interchange; Class I car hire and delay charges; interchange tracks fill within a day
manual_workaround: Paper interchange reports; consist files exchanged by secure email; joint yard inventory by walking the tracks
dependent_third_parties: TMS vendor; Class I partners' EDI services
quantified_operational_impact: About 410 cars a day interchanged; after 24 hours about 400 cars wait
quantified_regulatory_impact: Attended transfer and documentation for PIH cars in the HTUA (1580.205(c)) continue on paper
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: PIH cars left waiting in the HTUA increase exposure

description: Switch lists, yard inventory, and car placement at 5 yards and 2 transload terminals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Yard work slows to about half without switch lists; transload customers wait
manual_workaround: Printed yard inventory; handwritten switch lists; yard walk at shift change
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,900 car moves a day in the yards
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: car placement errors, including hazmat cars

business_process: Locomotive and car maintenance and FRA inspection records
description: Maintenance planning, daily locomotive inspection reports, car repair records; locomotive telemetry for AI-002
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Daily locomotive inspection reports may be written and must be retained (49 CFR 229.21); maintenance planning tolerates several days
manual_workaround: Paper inspection forms (already the legal record format); maintenance planning from the last printed schedule; AI-002 alerts paused
dependent_third_parties: Maintenance software vendor; locomotive telemetry vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 95 mechanical staff; locomotive shop; car repair shop
quantified_operational_impact: 118 locomotives inspected daily; scheduled maintenance slips about 1 day per day of outage
quantified_regulatory_impact: Inspection records must be complete; back-entry required
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: missed defect follow-up if records are lost

business_process: Track and structures inspection and maintenance planning
description: Track inspectors record required inspections and defects; AI-001 flags suspected defects for human review; work planning
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Required visual inspections continue regardless of systems (49 CFR 213.233); records can be kept on paper and entered later
manual_workaround: Paper inspection reports; AI-001 paused (it only supplements inspection); slow orders issued by radio and bulletin
dependent_third_parties: Track inspection software vendor; AI-001 vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Qualified track inspectors (49 CFR 213.7); 190 maintenance of way staff
quantified_operational_impact: 512 route miles inspected on regulatory cycles
quantified_regulatory_impact: Inspection records must be retained; back-entry required
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: a defect record lost before repair

business_process: Customer service, car tracing, and shipper portal
description: Shippers order cars, trace shipments, and submit bills of lading through the portal and EDI
process_owner: Director of Customer Service and Car Management
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer frustration and diversion to truck after 2 days; portal is part of the TMS
manual_workaround: Phone and email ordering; daily car location reports emailed to the top 40 shippers
quantified_operational_impact: 310 shippers; about 1,200 portal sessions a day

description: Freight billing from waybills, demurrage, accessorial charges, collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash timing, not revenue loss: about $586,000 of billing is delayed each day
manual_workaround: Bill from the last waybill extract after recovery; prioritize the top 40 accounts by hand
quantified_operational_impact: About $2.9 million of billing delayed at the MTD

business_process: Payroll and HR, including crew pay
description: Payroll for 850 employees, including crew pay calculated from hours and agreement rules; HR records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Missed or wrong crew pay damages labor relations; wage payment rules
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll and true up after recovery

business_process: Email, collaboration, and corporate file services
description: Email, chat, and file sharing for office staff; incident communications normally run here
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Coordination slows; the incident response plan assumes email may be compromised and uses out-of-band channels
manual_workaround: Out-of-band messaging group on company phones; printed call trees

business_process: Safety and hazmat incident reporting and emergency response coordination
description: Immediate telephone reports for reportable accidents and hazmat incidents; coordination with emergency responders
process_owner: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Telephone reports run on short clocks (49 CFR 225.9 immediate; 171.15 no later than 12 hours); emergency response needs hazmat car data
manual_workaround: Printed emergency contact lists and the hazmat security plan binder at both NOCs; phones independent of company systems
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat; on-duty Chief Dispatcher
quantified_operational_impact: Reportable events are rare (about 6 telephonic reports a year)
safety_impact_detail: Severe: delayed emergency response to a hazmat release

business_process: Procurement, accounts payable, and vendor management
description: Purchase orders, vendor payments, vendor contracts and security reviews
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Vendors tolerate a week of delay; business email compromise risk rises during outages
manual_workaround: Manual checks for urgent payments with call-back verification
